headline: ACC launches probe into Asif Mahmud over Ministry irregularities
summary: Former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud is the first from the interim administration to face an ACC inquiry into alleged corruption in recruitment and transfers.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials including former interim adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.
caption:
Asif Mahmud becomes the first former interim government adviser to face an ACC probe. Allegations include corruption in recruitment and transfers.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has launched an investigation into alleged corruption and irregularities at the Ministry of Youth and Sports, naming four officials including former interim adviser Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan.

headline: Govt employees' basic pay to rise by 100 to 142 percent under 9th Pay Scale
summary: The new pay scale significantly boosts public sector rewards, but experts warn it may widen the gap with the private sector and fuel a 'brain drain'.
details: The government has approved the ninth National Pay Scale, which will see basic pay across 20 grades rise by 100 to 142 percent. The raises are set to be rolled out in three phases, with the first phase beginning in July 2026.

The new scale provides predictability, pension benefits, and job security—advantages the private sector often lacks. Even entry-level grade-20 employees, such as support staff, will start with a basic salary of Tk 20,000, matching or exceeding the starting pay of many private-sector fresh graduates.

Concerns are rising that this disparity makes government jobs overwhelmingly attractive, potentially discouraging graduates from entering the private workforce or starting businesses. This could lead to more young professionals seeking opportunities abroad, contributing to the country's brain drain.

The private sector is currently struggling, with private investment falling to 21.53 percent of GDP by the end of FY2025-26. High interest rates, energy constraints, and economic uncertainty have made businesses more cautious about hiring and wage increases.

While the cabinet secretary suggested that private organizations raise salaries by 5 to 7 percent annually, the gap remains stark for low-wage workers. For instance, tea-garden workers are still fighting for a daily wage of Tk 500, while their current wage has remained at Tk 187 since 2022.
caption:
Basic pay for government employees is set to jump by up to 142%. But is this widening the gap with the private sector?
